# Vendored colour tokens

**Everything in this directory is generated by
[`noctua-colors`](../../../../noctua-colors) and copied here. Nothing in it is
edited in this repository, ever.**

## Regenerating

From the workspace root:

```sh
cd repos/noctua-colors
cargo xtask export
```

That command reads `specs/noctua.toml`, compiles it, and writes into every
consumer registered in that file. This directory is one of them — registered
there as:

```toml
[[consumers]]
name = "noctua-design"
path = "../noctua-design/packages/tokens/vendor"
targets = ["css", "tailwind", "json-ts", "rust"]
```

Four targets and not the rest: `css` and `tailwind` are what the components and
the documentation site style against, `json-ts` feeds anything that needs the
palette as data, and `rust` is what the Dioxus package compiles in. `scss`,
`qml`, `dtcg` and `reports` are not taken — nothing here consumes them, and an
unused target is payload plus review surface.

## Why it is vendored rather than depended on

`noctua-colors` has no published URL for a Rust consumer to depend on yet
(`NOCTUA.md §5.3`), and even once it does, vendoring keeps this repository
buildable with no network and no cross-repository version negotiation. The
switch to a git-tag or registry dependency is a one-line change when it is
worth making.

## The rule that matters

**This repository never defines a colour.** Not a hex, not an `oklch()`, not
"just this one shade". If a colour is missing, that is a one-line change in
`noctua-colors`' `specs/noctua.toml`, discussed first — `NOCTUA.md §8.8`.

A source gate enforces it: a colour literal anywhere in this repository's own
source fails `cargo xtask check`. This directory is excluded from that gate, for
the obvious reason that it is made of colour values, which is the entire point
of it.

## A measurement worth acting on

This directory is **73 MB**, and 56 MB of that is the `json-ts` target:

| Target | Size | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|
| `json` | 37 MB | nothing here yet |
| `ts` | 19 MB | nothing here yet |
| `css` | 14 MB | the components and the docs site |
| `rust` | 3.6 MB | the Dioxus package |
| `tailwind` | 132 KB | the Tailwind bridge |

`noctua-colors` excludes exactly that payload from its own npm package, for
exactly this reason — see its `package.json` `files` allowlist.

Dropping `json-ts` from this consumer's target list is a one-line change in
`noctua-colors`' `specs/noctua.toml`, and it is additive to reverse if the
documentation site later needs the palette as data. It is **not** made here:
`NOCTUA-PLAN.md` Stage 3 lists `noctua-colors` under "must NOT be touched", and
a target list is a decision for whoever owns that spec.
